flash_transcript: Board default cable overridden with dirtyJtag
Jtag frequency : requested 6000000 Hz -> real 6000000 Hz
methodology_note: Outer-loop manual flash attempt invoked after the operator power-cycle-reattached the GateMate A1-EVB-2M. The conductor had hit blocked_flash_failed across four consecutive autonomous iterations (exp2972, exp2984, exp2996, exp3008) plus exp3048's blocked_gatemate_output_contract_authority_missing. The direct command-line invocation, post-reattach, completed in under 5 seconds with openFPGALoader exit code 0 and the canonical Load SRAM via JTAG: 100.00% / Done success signal. This is the first successful GateMate bitstream flash recorded in the project. The bitstream is SRAM-based (volatile) and will be lost on power-cycle; a sample-level smoke test against /dev/uio or the equivalent host-visible IO path is the next step to close the Hardware-Task Continuity Discipline boundary.

field_principles.honest_verdict: Must start with success: prefix per Verdict Terminal-Prefix Discipline. The flash succeeded; the smoke test that would unlock the matrix-row promotion is downstream.
field_principles.inference_substrate: hardware_smoke per the Inference-Substrate Declaration Discipline. No LLM was invoked; the flash is a JTAG SRAM load.
field_principles.bitstream_sha256_flashed: Anchors what specifically was loaded; matches exp2956's recorded build sha256 exactly.
field_principles.duration_s: Wall-clock of the openFPGALoader invocation; ~4.5s is consistent with a 458KB SRAM load over 6MHz JTAG. The conductor's prior blocked_flash_failed verdicts likely hit before this stage.
field_principles.board_state_after_flash: openFPGALoader does not perform readback verification on this GateMate flow; the 100% load + Done status is the standard success signal. Downstream host-IO smoke test is required for stronger evidence.

what_changed_vs_prior_attempts: The operator power-cycle-reattached the board between exp3048 (.285) and this run. The DirtyJTAG re-enumerated at bus 3 device 15 (was device 6 on 2026-05-22, device 14 on 2026-05-23, no detection at exp3048 time). Whether the prior failures were USB-state-related, conductor-harness-invocation-related, or some combination is not determined by this single success; the diagnostic value of this artifact is that the direct invocation post-reattach works, establishing the upper bound on what success looks like.
next_steps: Run a host-IO smoke test against the flashed n=16 Ising tile: write spins via the bitstream's exposed I/O contract, read back the energy, measure per-sample wall-clock. This is the analog of what exp2898 did for KV260.
If the host-IO path is not yet implemented in the n=16 bitstream design, the GateMate continuity boundary remains open at the smoke-test stage even though the flash boundary is now closed.
Update research-hardware-wishlist.md's GateMate Active track entry to reflect 'flashed' status.
